as_told.title: Townsend Brown parachuting into Nazi Germany and the Stephenson telegram

plain: During the Second World War an American scientist named Thomas Townsend Brown is said to have parachuted behind enemy lines into Nazi Germany to bring back technology, and a telegram told his wife he had made it. The telegram is said to come from a man named William Stephenson and to be addressed to Brown's wife, Josephine Brown. Michels tells it several times. Once he credits a person named Jan Lundquist as his source. Another time he quotes the telegram as saying "your husband is okay" and calls the trip "a tech retrieval mission". Paul Schatzkin, a writer who has researched Brown's life, tells it through Brown's daughter, Linda Brown. He says the telegram was sent to her mother from the Rockefeller Plaza building in New York and "signed Intrepid, which was William Stephenson's name, code name." Those who tell it see it as a sign that Brown did secret wartime work far beyond his public career.
